claims.text: The proposed thermo-mechanical treatment will generate a stable dual-phase microstructure in HEAs.
The proposed thermo-mechanical treatment will refine the grains.
The treatment will produce uniformly dispersed nanoscale precipitates.
Typical as-cast HEAs relevant to the proposal have grain sizes of several hundred micrometers.
Homogenization at about 1000 °C for 2 h reduces compositional inhomogeneity and dendritic structure.
Hot rolling by approximately 50% refines the microstructure.
Rapid annealing at 800–900 °C for 30–60 s stabilizes a dual-phase structure.
An inert atmosphere is required to avoid oxidation during the treatment.
Severe plastic deformation increases dislocation density.
Grain refinement increases yield strength through Hall–Petch grain-boundary strengthening.
Rapid annealing promotes recovery.
A fine dual-phase arrangement maintains ductility by avoiding the brittleness associated with a single highly stiff phase.
Stable reinforcing precipitates increase Young's modulus.
Stable reinforcing precipitates increase fracture resistance.
The treatment will improve yield strength by approximately 10–20% relative to the as-cast state.
The treatment will improve fracture resistance by approximately 10–20% relative to the as-cast state.
The treatment will maintain or modestly increase ductility.
The treatment will maintain or modestly increase Young's modulus.
A high volume fraction of intrinsically brittle phases can prevent the proposed benefits.
Excessive thermal treatment can cause grain growth that negates the benefits.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis makes formation of a stable dual-phase structure central, whereas the directly relevant cited TMT record reports that all processed Zr7 MEA samples retained a single BCC structure irrespective of processing route.

The predicted outcome only requires ductility and Young's modulus to be maintained or modestly increased, but the falsification rule appears to require a 10–20% improvement in these properties along with yield strength and fracture resistance.
